tier_reason: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks is a well-known independent third-party suite. Its data.json at commit f673364 (2026-09-24) lists bun (framework_id 1189) at 145,896.6 req/s and nethttp (framework_id 811, Go stdlib http.ServeMux) at 67,239.1 req/s at 512 connections. The benchmark code (javascript/bun/cluster.ts, go/nethttp/main.go, javascript/bun.Dockerfile, go/Dockerfile) and build flags are public, but the CPU model is not reliably stated: cpu_name is a string hard-coded in .tasks/db.rake while uname reports x86_64. So B, not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: At 512 connections: Bun 145,896.6 req/s vs Go net/http (nethttp) 67,239.1 req/s, ~2.17x (derived from page data). Same run at 64 connections: 144,254.3 vs 71,498.7 (~2.02x). At 256 connections: 145,871.0 vs 67,381.9 (~2.16x). Each figure is the mean over the 3 contract routes. The older master-branch run (commit 0fccb1d, 2026-09-20, a different method) gives only 93,972.0 vs 83,963.5 at 512 connections (~1.12x) (derived from page data).
corrections.workload: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks route contract: GET / (empty body), GET /user/:id (returns the id), POST /user (empty body). Load is zrk --closed over keep-alive connections, 15-second runs at 64, 256 and 512 connections. The headline total_requests_per_s is the average over the 3 routes (avg() in the .tasks/db.rake export SQL). The server container used about 4 cores (server_cpu_cores 3.95 for Bun, 3.91 for net/http; saturation 98-99%). Bun runs Bun.serve with a routes table under node:cluster, one reusePort worker per core; Go runs net/http with http.ServeMux.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Bun: oven/bun:1.4-slim Docker image (javascript/bun.Dockerfile), 'bun install --production', 'bun run cluster.ts', Bun.serve development:false. data.json labels the Bun version 1.2.5 (from javascript/bun/config.yaml), which differs from the image tag. Go net/http: golang:1.27 image, CGO_ENABLED=1, 'go build -trimpath', GOAMD64=v3 when built for amd64 (go/Dockerfile).
corrections.hardware: CPU model not reliably stated. data.json hardware.cpu_name 'M1 Eight-Core Processor' and memory 7,733,008 are hard-coded constants in .tasks/db.rake. The live fields from Etc.uname report Linux 7.2.6-200.fc44.x86_64, machine x86_64, 16 host CPUs. The server container used about 4 cores.
corrections.license: MIT for Bun's own code, per LICENSE.md (GitHub reports NOASSERTION). Bun statically links JavaScriptCore/WebKit (LGPL-2) and tinycc (LGPL-2.1), plus permissive libraries such as BoringSSL, a uWebSockets fork and uSockets (Apache-2.0), mimalloc (MIT) and zstd (BSD OR GPL-2.0).
corrections.caveats: Numbers come from a third-party multi-language suite run on one unnamed host. The CPU model is unknown: data.json's cpu_name and memory are hard-coded in .tasks/db.rake, while uname reports Linux x86_64 with 16 CPUs. The ratio depends heavily on method: the older master-branch run (2026-09-20) shows only ~1.12x at 512 connections, and the README says results from different revisions are not comparable. The workload is a trivial 3-route API (empty body or path-parameter echo), so the gain measures HTTP-stack overhead, not application work. Bun runs as a node:cluster of reusePort workers. The Bun version label 1.2.5 in data.json differs from the oven/bun:1.4-slim image actually used. In the same run, Go fasthttp reaches 125,656.7 req/s at 512 connections, so Bun's margin over the fastest Go option is only ~1.16x. Bun's own code is MIT, but the binary statically links LGPL-2 JavaScriptCore/WebKit, which carries relinking obligations.

notes: The numbers match data.json exactly for Bun's own row and the nethttp row. benchmark_url was pinned to commit f673364 (identical SHA-1 content to develop HEAD). Bun appears in known_list.txt only because this record was merged; it has no separate earlier entry, so this is not a known-project duplicate. Metadata checked: 96,041 stars, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-09-26; usability 'mixed' kept, following the F-Stack precedent for a permissive core with statically linked copyleft parts.
